page: Vultr vhp-1c-2gb-amd is a virtual private server belonging to the High Performance family, configured with 1 shared AMD EPYC vCPU operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The single-core processor features 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions, AES cryptography, and secure virtualization via AMD SVM. System memory is limited to 2.0 GB of RAM, and local storage is provided by a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not feature any dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core compute capabilities and overall system throughput. The shared AMD EPYC core achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core CPU tests and strong results in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, because the instance is constrained to a single shared vCPU, multi-core CPU performance is weak, and Passmark CPU physics and overall CPU scores fall into the bottom tier. Memory performance is also limited, with read-only bandwidth and Passmark memory scores ranking in the lowest percentiles, though large-block write bandwidth and single-threaded gzip compression maintain average performance levels.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server represents an entry-level, budget-friendly tier that trades resource density and multi-threaded performance for low-cost access to NVMe storage and modern AMD EPYC instruction sets. Due to poor database operations, low redis SET throughput, and weak static web serving benchmarks, it is poorly suited for production databases or high-traffic web applications. Instead, the server is best utilized for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic development environments, simple automation scripts, or low-demand background utilities that do not require sustained multi-core execution or high memory bandwidth.
